A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IC-Custom. All supplied pages, including equations, Tables 1–3 and supplementary Figures 6–9, are readable and matchable despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original ProductBench and DreamBench experiments, a human preference study, multi-reference evaluations and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results in Tables 2–3 and Figures 4–9, alongside illustrative customization outputs.

M1.justification: The polyptych inputs, velocity-prediction objective, ICMA task tokens and boundary embeddings remain unchanged in Sections 3.3–3.4. The LoRA configuration and two-stage training procedure are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same real-product and synthetic training sources, ProductBench, DreamBench, and position-aware, position-free and multi-reference tasks. Revised sample counts and replacement teaser examples do not establish additional domain or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership within the corresponding experiments is unchanged. Table 2 and Figures 4–5 retain FLUX-Fill+Redux, OminiCtrl, DreamO, Insert Anything and GPT-4o, with the same task-specific inclusions and exclusions.

E3.justification: Section 3.5 revises synthetic diptychs from 2,787 to 4K and the diptych total from 11K to 12K. Polyptychs change from 2,137 real plus 2,787 synthetic samples to 2K plus 2K. These are reported training-data count changes within retained coverage; the PDFs do not establish retraining. Evaluation procedures, metrics, training iterations and human-study settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The reference-count analysis and zero-shot, input-layer, real-data and user-mask ablations remain unchanged in Sections 4.4 and 4.6, Table 3 and Figures 7–8. The replacement Figure 1 illustrates existing capabilities without adding a distinct analytical question.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run variability, seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. Human-preference percentages and GPT-4o voting results retain the same statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figure 1 replaces qualitative result entries with dress-transfer and toy-scene examples and removes the earlier sunglasses multi-reference example. Numerical results in Tables 2–3 and Figure 7, and the remaining qualitative Figures 4–9, are unchanged. No numerical performance gain is reported.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 and their mathematical content are retained, with no new assumptions, derivations or proofs. Adding the missing membership symbol in the text-token shape declaration repairs notation without changing the definition.

C1.justification: The abstract revises the dataset contribution from 12K samples comprising 8K real and 4K synthetic samples to 16K comprising 10K real and 6K synthetic samples. The central claims about unified customization, ICMA, comparative performance and parameter efficiency remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of baseline failures, real-data benefits, mask-training effects and multi-reference behavior are retained. Section 5 states the same limitation concerning explicit viewpoint and lighting consistency.

D1.justification: The introduction and Section 3.5 revise and clarify the documented real/synthetic composition and diptych/polyptych totals. Data sources, filtering and annotation procedures, implementation hyperparameters, resolution buckets and project-access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and cited works are retained, including the positioning relative to concurrent ACE++ and FLUX.1 Kontext. Bibliographic differences concern back-reference page numbers rather than added research or changed positioning.

P1.justification: The dataset paragraphs in the introduction and Section 3.5 are rewritten to distinguish diptychs and polyptychs and explain their totals. Other prose and the section sequence remain substantially unchanged, apart from a small notation correction and reflow.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned from a dense three-task gallery into two larger position-aware and position-free panels; its unchanged caption still mentions multi-reference examples. Table 3 moves from page 8 to page 9, while the remaining figures and tables retain their designs and the supplementary pages shift with pagination.

improvement.justification: The abstract, introduction and Section 3.5 now consistently distinguish 12K diptychs and 4K polyptychs, reducing v1's conflicting dataset accounting. This provides a limited clarity and reproducibility benefit without changing the quantitative evidence or establishing retraining. The benefit is partly offset by Figure 1 losing its explicit multi-reference demonstration while retaining a caption that describes one.
